Priors for a bayesnec model

Source: R/get_priors.R
get_priors.Rd

Returns priors in the form bnec accepts them, either from a fit that has already been run or from a formula and data before anything is fitted.

get_priors(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'formula'
get_priors(
  object,
  data,
  family = NULL,
  prior_type = "uninformative",
  model_survival = NULL,
  ...
)

Arguments

object

An object of class bayesnecfit, bayesmanecfit or bayesnechurdlefit as returned by bnec; or a bayesnecformula, a formula or a character string that can be coerced to one.

...

Unused.

data

A data.frame containing the data referred to by the formula.

family

A family function, as passed to bnec. If NULL (the default) it is chosen from the data the way bnec would.

prior_type

A character string, either "uninformative" (the default) or "regularizing". See bnec.

model_survival

An optional character string naming the equation for the second block of a joint hurdle or zero-inflated fit. See bnec.

Value

For a single model, an object of class brmsprior. For a model set, a named list of them, one per model, named as bnec expects a named prior list to be. For a bayesnechurdlefit, a list of two such objects, one per component.

Details

Two entry points, answering two different questions.

Given a fit, get_priors returns the priors that fit actually used, including any the user overrode. This is the record of what was run: bnec(formula, data = data, prior = get_priors(fit)) reproduces the same model.

Given a formula and data, it returns the priors bnec would generate, without fitting anything, so they can be inspected and edited before the first run. The family is chosen from the data exactly as bnec would unless one is supplied, and models invalid for it are dropped with the same message.

The two can disagree, and that is the point of having both: once a prior has been overridden, the fit's priors are no longer the ones the defaults would produce. Given the same formula, data and family, and no user prior, they agree.

What is returned is the population-level priors on the parameters of the model's own non-linear formula, which are the ones bnec accepts through prior. Where a disp term adds a variance function on the fitted mean – disp("power") and the other named forms – its parameters (c0, c1, ...) belong to that formula and come back with the curve parameters. They are needed: bnec takes a supplied prior whole, so a set handed back without them leaves brms to put a flat prior on each, which is a different model. See bayesnecformula.

What is left to brms and its defaults, and so is not returned, is the family's own dispersion parameter (sigma, shape, phi) where dispersion is held constant, and the linear predictor of a disp(~x) sub-model. Neither can be supplied through bnec(prior = ) in any case, because the initial-value search matches prior names against the model's own parameters and rejects any prior naming one outside that set.

This is why get_priors is not pull_prior, which returns the whole brmsprior a fit carries – brms defaults, duplicated vectorized rows and all – and is for looking at rather than for feeding back in.

See also

bnec, pull_prior, check_priors, show_params

Examples

library(bayesnec)
data(manec_example)
# the priors a fit used, ready to pass back to bnec(prior = )
get_priors(manec_example)
#> $nec4param
#>                                        prior class coef group resp dpar nlpar
#>                                 normal(0, 5)     b                       beta
#>  normal(-0.475731934041565, 3.6135432617749)     b                        bot
#>                   gamma(5, 2.28313180499098)     b                        nec
#>    normal(2.63236428713204, 3.6135432617749)     b                        top
#>                lb               ub source
#>              <NA>             <NA>   user
#>              <NA>             <NA>   user
#>  0.03234801324009 3.22051966293556   user
#>              <NA>             <NA>   user
#> 
#> $ecx4param
#>                                        prior class coef group resp dpar nlpar
#>                                 normal(0, 5)     b                       beta
#>  normal(-0.475731934041565, 3.6135432617749)     b                        bot
#>                   gamma(5, 2.28313180499098)     b                       ec50
#>    normal(2.63236428713204, 3.6135432617749)     b                        top
#>                lb               ub source
#>              <NA>             <NA>   user
#>              <NA>             <NA>   user
#>  0.03234801324009 3.22051966293556   user
#>              <NA>             <NA>   user
#> 
# the priors bayesnec would generate, without fitting anything
get_priors(y ~ crf(x, "nec3param"), data = nec_data)
#>                       prior class coef group resp dpar nlpar               lb
#>                normal(0, 5)     b                       beta             <NA>
#>                  beta(5, 2)     b                        top                0
#>  gamma(5, 2.28313180499098)     b                        nec 0.03234801324009
#>                ub tag source
#>              <NA>       user
#>                 1       user
#>  3.22051966293556       user
